children: This refers to the news report ‘Jio Platforms IPO draws record ₹2.50 lakh crore institutional demand’ (Oct 20). It is heartening to see investors placing strong trust in an Indian company despite competition from powerful international players. The overwhelming institutional response to Jio Platforms reflects the confidence in India’s digital growth and the ability of domestic enterprises to compete on an international scale.

The participation of Indian mutual funds, insurance companies and international investors is encouraging. However, strong demand alone should not determine an investment decision. Retail investors must examine the company’s valuation, financial performance and future prospects before subscribing. Transparent disclosures and fair pricing are essential to protect their interests. India needs more home-grown companies that attract global capital, generate employment and promote innovation. This will strengthen our economy and enhance India’s position in the global marketplace.

This refers to ‘Is Trump’s diesel deal another poll gimmick?’ (Oct19). Yes, of course. Mind you, his Republican senators seeking re-election even in the safe seats, are highly likely to find it extremely hard to make a comeback. But then, credit for such a worrisome scenario goes to Trump for he is known for taking U turns, much to the discomfiture of others as well as his fellow citizens. The biggest fallout of Trump’s tariff-driven salvos is that he may end up scoring a self goal in the process. The case in example could be the full-fledged retaliation by Canada in response to his tariff-centric tactics.

With reference to ‘Ecosystem services and role of farmers’ (Oct19), the writers’ concern on vital areas connected to agriculture on issues such as groundwater recharge, carbon storage and pollination are very valid. Free power for agriculture has resulted in the overexploitation of of ground water. The lack of contiguous agricultural fields and fast urbanisation affect cross-pollination, which will have an impact on the quality and quantity of the produce.

The PM Programme for Restoration, Awareness Generation, Nourishment and Amelioration of Mother Earth,or PM-PRANAM, aimed at reducing the use of chemical fertilizers and promoting balanced, sustainable agriculture, is losing sheen. The per-acre incentive prescribed for direct-seed technique, which helps in reducing the use of irrigation water by 15-20 per cent, needs to be reviewed and taken to other rice-producing States for a wider coverage. Organic agriculture is yet to take shape to have a visible impact on import of chemicalised fertilizers. The government could launch a ‘gains from grains’ campaign with all incentives, subsidies and other promotional schemes under one roof.

A film star’s charm can open doors, but only a government’s work keeps them open (Reel charm of Vijay, Oct19). When a CEO jokes about blockbusters, while announcing a ₹2,000 crore project, it shows that Tamil Nadu has won attention. Attention, however, does not mean employment. Every major investment should come with a public ‘jobs promise sheet,’ listing how many local people will be hired and what skills will be taught, with a yearly update for citizens. Popularity is a gift that should be used with care. A leader loved by the crowds can bring investors, but investors stay for stable rules and skilled workers, reliable power and quick approvals. Fans, in turn, can show their affection by asking questions, not just cheering. When applause is matched by accountability, charm becomes governance.
